dynamicTools.name: ask
dynamicTools.description: Use this tool instead of the question tool, and wherever instructions say the question tool. Ask the user questions and wait for the answers. Prefer this over guessing whenever a choice is the user's to make. The user never sees your thinking or your tool results: anything a question points at, such as a plan, summary, research findings, list or image, must be in your reply above this call or in `context`. `context`: Markdown shown in the chat right above the question; put there what the user has to read to answer, such as the explanation, plan or findings, and leave it empty only when your reply above already says it or the question needs nothing more. `questions`: one or more pages, each a question with a short `header` and 2–4 options (`label`, optional `description` only when the label needs it). Put the recommended option first and end its label with "(Recommended)". Set `multiSelect` when several answers can be true. An option may carry `image`, a PNG, JPG or SVG file path, shown beside the list: use it when a picture explains the option better than words. Set `gallery: true` on a page to show 2–4 designs side by side when the choice is between visual directions; every option then needs an image. `matrix` instead of `questions`: several short propositions answered on one shared scale (2–4 steps, ending in an uncertainty step such as "Unsure"); ask the rows answered with it again later, one by one. The user can always type their own answer and add a note; `[Image N: path]` in an answer or note is a picture they pasted, so read that file.

context.description: Markdown the user reads in the chat before answering; may be empty.

header.description: A short label for the page bar.

image.description: Path of a PNG, JPG or SVG file, absolute or relative to the project.

skills.name: imagegen
skills.description: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas.

interface.defaultPrompt: Use $imagegen to make or edit an image for this project.
